name: Transit stops, stations and terminals (count)
plain: How many places to board public transit lie inside the municipality: stops, stations and ferry terminals from public timetables, plus stops, stations and terminals that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap. It counts places to board, not routes or trips.
definition: Count of mapped transit features inside the municipality of five kinds: transit stop, bus stop, bus station, rail station and ferry terminal (see municipalities.stop_kinds). It adds (1) every boarding point in the public timetable feeds (GTFS, the General Transit Feed Specification) of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and the municipal transit systems, and (2) OpenStreetMap bus stops, bus stations, rail stations and ferry terminals that do not duplicate a scheduled stop. Airports, taxi stands and EV (electric vehicle) chargers are not counted. The scheduled part is the field gtfs_stops; the rest comes only from OpenStreetMap.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, which counts the stops in transport.json again (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: The build reads every GTFS feed (network.py, which also gives each scheduled stop its kind) and an OpenStreetMap query for bus stops, bus stations, railway and public-transport stations and ferry terminals (transport.py). An OpenStreetMap bus stop, bus station, rail station or ferry terminal is dropped when the nearest scheduled stop is less than 30 m away. OpenStreetMap stations and terminals are also dropped when a scheduled or already kept feature of the same kind lies less than 200 m away (rail stations, ferry terminals) or less than 100 m away (bus stations), because one station is often mapped as several points. Each remaining feature goes to the municipality whose boundary contains it; a point outside every boundary, such as a pier over water, goes to the municipality whose boundary is nearest. The field is the number of features per municipality.
source_detail: ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) GTFS feed and municipal GTFS feeds (National RTAP, Rural Transit Assistance Program, portal), read by network.py; OpenStreetMap extract of 1 October 2026 (Overpass API, application programming interface), read by transport.py; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: A higher count means more places to board. This is a count, not a rate: large and dense municipalities have more stops, and so do places where volunteers have mapped more. The observatory publishes no stops-per-resident rate; for a size-adjusted measure of residents, use pop_served_pct. The count does not measure how often vehicles come, whether a timetable is still valid, or whether people can reach a stop. A value of 0 means no stop appears in these sources; it does not rule out públicos (shared taxis) or informal service that nobody mapped. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 4,360 such features: 2,881 in a timetable that has not ended, 966 in a timetable that has ended and 513 that come only from OpenStreetMap (see stops_current, stops_expired and stops_osm).
caveats: Scheduled stops stay in the count when the operator's timetable has ended (966 of them in the 2026-10 snapshot; see stops_expired and municipalities.feed_status).
OpenStreetMap is mapped by volunteers, so coverage is uneven. Its data carry the ODbL (Open Database License); read the license before reusing them.
A stop counts in the municipality where it stands, not where its riders live.
Stop records are not merged within a feed or across feeds, so one physical stop with two records counts twice (see municipalities.gtfs_stops).
The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it. ATI provides its feed as is, without warranty.
The nightly refresh counts the stops again from transport.json, so the scheduled part follows the feeds. The OpenStreetMap part changes only at a full build (see municipalities.transit_data_updates).

name: Scheduled stops from timetable feeds (count)
plain: How many boarding points inside the municipality appear in a public timetable. The timetable comes from the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) or from a municipal transit system.
definition: Count of features inside the municipality whose source is the ATI GTFS feed or a municipal GTFS feed. GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) is the standard format for public timetable data; ATI is the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado. A feature is a boarding point in the feed's stops file (location type blank or 0) with coordinates inside Puerto Rico. The ATI feed covers Tren Urbano, the buses of AMA (Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses) and the AcuaExpreso ferries. Bus stations, rail stations and ferry terminals are included when the feed lists them as stops. Each stop record in a feed counts once, even if no trip serves it on a typical weekday and even if the feed's timetable has expired. It is the scheduled part of transit_stops.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, which counts the stops in transport.json again (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: network.py reads each feed's stops, routes, trips and stop times. A stop whose longitude lacks its minus sign (Jayuya's feed) is corrected, a stop outside Puerto Rico's bounds is dropped, and each remaining stop gets a kind (see municipalities.stop_kinds). transport.py assigns each stop to the municipality whose boundary contains it (or, when it falls outside every boundary, the municipality whose boundary is nearest) and counts the stops whose source is the ATI feed or a municipal feed.
source_detail: ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) GTFS feed (PRITA_GTFS.zip) and the municipal GTFS feeds (24 in the 2026-10 snapshot) listed in the registry of the National RTAP (Rural Transit Assistance Program) portal; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: A scheduled stop has a published timetable entry. The count says nothing about how often vehicles stop there. It is a count, not a rate: large and dense municipalities have more stops. Municipalities with no feed of their own show 0 unless another operator's stops fall inside them. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 3,847 scheduled stop records, and one of them has no trip on a typical weekday. Of these, 2,881 are in a timetable that has not ended and 966 in one that has ended (stops_current and stops_expired add up to this field).
caveats: Stops of expired timetables stay in the count: 7 municipal feeds had expired when the transit data were built on 2026-10-02 (966 stops; see stops_expired).
The observatory has no real-time data. A scheduled stop shows that the timetable lists it, not that vehicles ran.

Records are not merged within a feed or across feeds. In the 2026-10 snapshot, at least 190 of the 3,847 records repeat a location already used by another record of the same feed (coordinates equal to four decimals, about 11 m), for example separate boarding and alighting records. The count is of records, not distinct places. One physical stop that two operators list also counts twice.

The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it. ATI provides its feed as is, without warranty, and its terms ask apps built on it to say they are not affiliated with ATI. The observatory is not affiliated with or sponsored by ATI.
The nightly refresh rewrites the scheduled stops and counts them again, so this field follows the feeds (see municipalities.transit_data_updates).

name: Stops with a current timetable (count)
plain: How many of the municipality's stops, stations and terminals are in a published timetable that has not ended. With the next two counts it splits transit_stops by the state of the timetable.
definition: Count of the features counted in transit_stops (kinds transit stop, bus stop, bus station, rail station and ferry terminal) that are scheduled stops (stops in the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feed of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, or of a municipal system) of an operator whose feed has an end date on or after access_as_of. stops_current + stops_expired = gtfs_stops, and stops_current + stops_expired + stops_osm = transit_stops in each of the 78 municipalities. A stop belongs to the municipality where it stands, not to its operator's.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); the files are rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the state of each timetable is judged as of 2026-10-06 (see access_as_of).

method: access.py sorts each stop of the five kinds by the state of its operator's feed on the as-of date: current (feed end date not before the as-of date), expired (a scheduled stop of a feed that has ended or has no end date) or mapped by volunteers (source OpenStreetMap). It then counts them in each municipality.
source_detail: transport.json (ATI and municipal GTFS feeds read on 2026-10-02) and feed end dates from operators.json; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: A count, not a rate: large and dense municipalities have more stops. It shows where stops with a timetable in force are. It does not show how often vehicles come. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 2,881, in 30 municipalities (San Juan 1,009, Guaynabo 349, Bayamón 276, Carolina 268); 48 municipalities have 0. The Municipality tab shows the three counts in one line.
caveats: The state is judged on the as-of date and changes on the day a feed ends: on that date the stops of the operator move from current to expired. In the 2026-10 snapshot 9 of the 18 current feeds end between 2026-10-31 and 2027-01-31.
Stop records are not merged within a feed or across feeds, so one physical stop with two records counts twice (see municipalities.gtfs_stops).
A timetable that has not ended is not proof of service. The observatory has no real-time data.
The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it. ATI provides its feed as is, without warranty.

name: Stops with an expired timetable (count)
plain: How many of the municipality's stops, stations and terminals are in a published timetable that has ended. The stop may still be served, but its published timetable no longer covers today.
definition: Count of the features counted in transit_stops that are scheduled stops (stops in the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feed of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, or of a municipal system) of an operator whose feed ended before access_as_of, or has no end date. Stops of a feed that has ended stay in transit_stops, gtfs_stops, transit_pct and pop_served_pct. They are left out of stops_current, of the acc_ fields (except acc_paper_pct, which counts the places near them) and of pop_served_active_pct.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); the files are rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the state of each timetable is judged as of 2026-10-06 (see access_as_of).

method: access.py counts, in each municipality, the scheduled stops of the five kinds whose operator's feed end date is before the as-of date (or missing). See municipalities.stops_current.
source_detail: transport.json (ATI and municipal GTFS feeds read on 2026-10-02) and feed end dates from operators.json; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 966 such stops, in 10 municipalities: Caguas 291, Ponce 276, San Lorenzo 159, Juncos 128, Fajardo 81, Cidra 14, Hatillo 11, Gurabo 4, Carolina 1 and Las Piedras 1. They belong to 7 operators whose feeds ended: Ponce on 2024-12-31, Hatillo on 2025-12-31, Cidra on 2026-01-15, Caguas on 2026-01-31, San Lorenzo on 2026-02-28, Fajardo on 2026-06-15 and Juncos on 2026-07-31. A stop can lie in a neighboring municipality: Gurabo has no feed of its own. A feed can run out of dates while buses still run, so a large count is not proof that service stopped.
caveats: The state is judged on the as-of date. Renewing a feed moves its stops to stops_current at the next run.
Stop records are not merged, so one physical stop with two records counts twice (see municipalities.gtfs_stops).
The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it.

name: Stops mapped only by volunteers, with no timetable (count)
plain: How many of the municipality's stops, stations and terminals appear only in OpenStreetMap, where volunteers mapped them. The observatory holds no timetable for them.
definition: Count of the features counted in transit_stops whose source is OpenStreetMap: bus stops, bus stations and ferry terminals that do not duplicate a scheduled stop (see municipalities.transit_stops for the rules that remove duplicates). They have no timetable, so they are neither current nor expired.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); the files are rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the state of each timetable is judged as of 2026-10-06 (see access_as_of).

method: access.py counts, in each municipality, the stops of the five kinds whose source is OpenStreetMap. The OpenStreetMap points are read only at a full build.
source_detail: OpenStreetMap extract of 1 October 2026 (Overpass API), kept as in transport.json; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 513 such stops (459 bus stops, 47 bus stations and 7 ferry terminals), in 47 municipalities: Carolina 185, San Juan 177, Bayamón 44, Guaynabo 17 and Toa Baja 15 have the most. A high count shows where volunteers mapped many stops. It is not a measure of service.
caveats: Volunteers map unevenly, so a municipality with few such stops may simply be mapped less. Points can be missing, out of date or wrong; the observatory does not check them on the ground.
OpenStreetMap data carry the ODbL (Open Database License); read the license before reusing them.
Most of the volunteer-mapped bus stations are públicos (shared taxi) terminals, for which the observatory holds no timetable.

name: Bus stations and terminals (count)
plain: How many bus stations and terminals are mapped inside the municipality, from public timetable feeds and from OpenStreetMap. It counts records, not buildings.
definition: Count of features of kind bus station: (1) scheduled stops that no rail or ferry route serves and whose name starts with Terminal or Estación (from the feed of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, ATI, or from municipal feeds), and (2) OpenStreetMap features tagged amenity=bus_station, or public_transport=station without a railway tag, after removing those less than 100 m from a scheduled or already kept bus station. Bus stations are also part of transit_stops.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, which counts the stops in transport.json again (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: A scheduled stop becomes a bus station only by its name: the build tests whether the stop name starts with Terminal or Estación (the accent is optional, but a letter missing from the name is not tolerated). OpenStreetMap features are kept when no scheduled stop lies less than 30 m away and no scheduled or already kept bus station lies less than 100 m away. Each feature is assigned to the municipality whose boundary contains it.
source_detail: GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stop names (ATI and municipal feeds); OpenStreetMap tags amenity=bus_station and public_transport=station (extract of 1 October 2026); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: Use it to see where a town has a central terminal. It is a count, not a rate: larger municipalities and places with more mapping have more. It does not say how many routes the terminal serves, and a count of 8 can be eight records of one terminal. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 91 bus stations: 44 scheduled stops (15 from the ATI feed, 29 from municipal feeds) and 47 from OpenStreetMap. Overture Maps lists 24 places as bus stations in the 2026-10 snapshot (see places.type.transportation); that is a count of place listings, not of the stations counted here.
caveats: The scheduled-stop rule rests on the stop name alone. A stop named Terminal counts as a station whatever it looks like, and a station with another name is missed. In some municipal feeds the accented letter is missing from the name. Examples from the 2026-10 snapshot: San Lorenzo's feed has 8 stops, all named "Terminal" and all at one location, so all 8 count. In Canóvanas, "Estacin Multimodal" stays an ordinary stop. In Guaynabo, "Estacion tren Torrimar" counts as a bus station about 160 m from the rail station "Estación Torrimar", so one place counts twice.

Counts records, not buildings. In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan's 13 include a boarding record and an alighting record of the same terminal (Sagrado Corazón) and two records with the same name, "Estacion Martinez Nadal".
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 39 of the 47 OpenStreetMap bus stations have público or pública in the name (33 say Carros Públicos, shared-taxi terminals); the observatory holds no timetable for them.

Until the 2026-11 fix, the ATI terminal named Terminal de Cataño was counted in San Juan: it falls just outside every municipal boundary, and the build gave such a point the municipality with the nearest center point, so Cataño showed 0. It now takes the nearest boundary and counts in Cataño.
OpenStreetMap is mapped by volunteers, so coverage is uneven. Its data carry the ODbL (Open Database License); read the license before reusing them.

The nightly refresh counts the stations again from transport.json, so the scheduled stations follow the feeds. The OpenStreetMap stations change only at a full build (see municipalities.transit_data_updates).

name: Rail stations (count)
plain: How many train stations lie inside the municipality. In the 2026-10 snapshot they are all Tren Urbano stations.
definition: Count of scheduled stops served by a rail route (GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, route types 1, 2 and 12), plus OpenStreetMap railway stations that lie 200 m or more from a scheduled or kept rail station. Trams (route type 0) are not rail in this count. Rail stations are also part of transit_stops.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, which counts the stops in transport.json again (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: A scheduled stop is a rail station when at least one route that serves it has a rail route type in the feed. OpenStreetMap stations tagged railway=station (or public_transport=station with a railway tag) are dropped when a scheduled stop lies less than 30 m away or a rail station lies less than 200 m away. Each station is assigned to the municipality whose boundary contains it.
source_detail: ATI GTFS feed (Tren Urbano); OpenStreetMap railway=station (extract of 1 October 2026); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 16 rail stations. All come from the feed of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI): San Juan 12, Bayamón 3, Guaynabo 1. No OpenStreetMap station remains after duplicates are removed. Only three municipalities have a rail station, so 0 is the normal value.
caveats: Counts stations, not lines or service.
The nightly refresh counts the stations again from transport.json, so a change in the ATI feed shows at the next run (see municipalities.transit_data_updates).

name: Ferry terminals (count)
plain: How many ferry terminals are mapped inside the municipality. Some come from the public timetable of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and some from OpenStreetMap.
definition: Count of ferry terminal features: (1) scheduled stops served by a ferry route in the ATI feed and (2) OpenStreetMap features tagged amenity=ferry_terminal that lie 200 m or more from a scheduled or kept terminal. Ferry terminals are also part of transit_stops.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, which counts the stops in transport.json again (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: A scheduled stop is a ferry terminal when it is served by a ferry route (GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, route type 4) and no rail route serves it. OpenStreetMap terminals are dropped when a scheduled stop lies less than 30 m away or a terminal lies less than 200 m away. A terminal over water has no containing boundary, so it goes to the municipality whose boundary is nearest.
source_detail: ATI GTFS feed; OpenStreetMap amenity=ferry_terminal (extract of 1 October 2026); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: A ferry terminal marks a boat connection. This is a count, not a rate, and it does not tell which routes or how many sailings serve the terminal. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 13 ferry terminals: 6 from the ATI feed and 7 from OpenStreetMap.
caveats: OpenStreetMap ferry terminals can include other piers. In the 2026-10 snapshot they include a cruise-ship pier in San Juan and two terminals with no name.

A terminal over water belongs to the municipality whose boundary is nearest. Until the 2026-11 fix it went to the municipality with the nearest center point, which can differ from the municipality the service is named for: the Cataño ferry terminal (and the Cataño bus terminal) was counted in San Juan, and Cataño showed 0 ferry terminals. Both now count in Cataño.
OpenStreetMap is mapped by volunteers, so coverage is uneven. Its data carry the ODbL (Open Database License); read the license before reusing them.

name: Airports and aerodromes (count)
plain: How many airports and airfields lie inside the municipality, from the list of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and from OpenStreetMap. It includes small, private, historic and seaplane facilities.
definition: Count of airport features inside the municipality: the Puerto Rico airports in the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) list, public and private use, plus OpenStreetMap features tagged aeroway=aerodrome that lie 2 km or more from every FAA airport. Helipads are not counted.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build. The nightly transit refresh counts again from transport.json, but the points in it (FAA list and OpenStreetMap) are read only at a full build, so the value changes only then.

method: FAA airports with state code PR come from the BTS (Bureau of Transportation Statistics) NTAD (National Transportation Atlas Database). OpenStreetMap aerodromes less than 2 km from an FAA airport are treated as the same airport and dropped. Each remaining feature is assigned to the municipality whose boundary contains it.
source_detail: FAA airports via BTS NTAD (layer Airports_, state code PR; list downloaded 1 October 2026, 14 airports); OpenStreetMap aeroway=aerodrome (extract of 1 October 2026); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: The count is of facilities, not of airlines or flights, and it is not a rate. A value of 1 can mean a large commercial airport or a small airfield. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 25 airports: 14 from the FAA list and 11 from OpenStreetMap. Overture Maps also lists 120 places under its airport category in the 2026-10 snapshot; that is a count of place listings, not of airports (see places.type.transportation).
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, the OpenStreetMap aerodromes include seaplane bases, historic and military airfields, and one whose name says it is closed (Patillas, marked CERRADO). They all count.

Counts follow the map pin, not the FAA city: in the 2026-10 snapshot Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport is listed under San Juan by the FAA but its coordinates fall in Carolina, so Carolina counts it.
OpenStreetMap is mapped by volunteers, so coverage is uneven. Its data carry the ODbL (Open Database License); read the license before reusing them.

name: Public-use airports (count)
plain: How many of the municipality's airports the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lists as open to the public. Airports known only from OpenStreetMap are not counted here.
definition: Count of FAA airports inside the municipality whose FAA use code is PU (public use). It is a subset of airports. Airports with the FAA use code PR (private use) are not counted as public use.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build. The nightly transit refresh counts again from transport.json, but the points in it (FAA list and OpenStreetMap) are read only at a full build, so the value changes only then.

method: The build sets a public-use flag for each FAA record when its use code (fac_use) equals PU, then counts flagged airports per municipality. OpenStreetMap aerodromes carry no such flag in this dataset and are never counted.
source_detail: FAA airports via BTS (Bureau of Transportation Statistics) NTAD (National Transportation Atlas Database), field fac_use = PU; list downloaded 1 October 2026; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: Use it to see where the FAA lists an airport open to the public. It does not say whether airlines serve it. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 10 public-use airports among its 14 FAA airports; the other four (in Adjuntas, Cabo Rojo, Lajas and Vega Baja) are private use.
caveats: An airport known only from OpenStreetMap is not counted because its record has no public-use flag. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Fajardo's Aeropuerto Diego Jiménez Torres (code FAJ) is in the data only through OpenStreetMap, because the FAA list the observatory uses does not include it, so Fajardo shows 2 airports and 0 public ones.
The value follows the FAA list at the date of the build; the FAA can change a facility's status.

name: Tourism places within 400 m of a rail station or ferry terminal (%)
plain: Out of every 100 tourism places in the municipality, how many are within 400 m of a train station or a ferry terminal. It marks places near a rail or boat connection.
definition: The number of tourism places in the municipality whose distance to the nearest rail station or ferry terminal is 400 m or less, divided by the tourism places counted (access_n), times 100, rounded to one decimal. The stations and terminals come from any source: the timetable feeds of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and OpenStreetMap, whatever the state of the timetable. Bus stations and airports are not counted.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); the files are rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the access is as of 2026-10-06 (see access_as_of).

method: access.py tests the distance from each place to every point of kind rail station or ferry terminal in transport.json, counts the places within 400 m in each municipality and divides by the counted places.
source_detail: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026); rail stations and ferry terminals from transport.json (the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, feed of ATI read on 2026-10-02; OpenStreetMap extract of 1 October 2026); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: A high value means many of the municipality's visitor places are near a station or terminal where a train or a boat starts. It does not say whether service runs, or whether the connection leads where a visitor wants to go. In the 2026-10 snapshot the value is 2.9% island-wide (695 of 24,209 places) and ranges from 0.0 to 23.5 (Culebra). Only 9 municipalities have a value above 0: Culebra 23.5, Cataño 16.2, San Juan 14.5, Vieques 11.4, Bayamón 9.5, Ceiba 2.3, Fajardo 1.7, Guaynabo 1.7 and Arecibo 0.5.
caveats: The ferry terminals include volunteer-mapped points. For example, a cruise-ship pier in San Juan counts (see municipalities.ferry_terminals).
A rail station or ferry terminal can have an expired timetable, or none. Read this field with acc_cur400_pct.
Straight-line distance, not a walking route. Públicos, taxis, ride-hailing and rental cars are not counted.
A municipality with few places can swing widely: the smallest has 36 places, so one place is 2.8 points. Check access_n before you compare shares.
Counts are listings from Overture Maps, not businesses, rooms or visitors.
A municipality with no stop counted inside its border (14 in the 2026-10 snapshot) holds the stored value, which is not a measured share. The downloaded municipality table leaves it blank.
example: In the 2026-10 snapshot: Culebra 23.5% (its ferry terminal); San Juan 14.5%; Ponce 0.0%.

name: Tourism places within 400 m of only an expired or unscheduled stop (%)
plain: Out of every 100 tourism places in the municipality, how many are within 400 m of a mapped stop but of no stop with a current timetable. The stop's timetable has ended, or volunteers mapped the stop and no timetable exists.
definition: The number of tourism places in the municipality that have a mapped stop of any kind within 400 m (transit_400m) but no stop with a current timetable within 400 m (ts_m above 400), divided by the tourism places counted (access_n), times 100, rounded to one decimal. Apart from rounding it equals transit_pct minus acc_cur400_pct. Such a place rests on a stop in a feed that has ended, or on a stop that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap with no timetable.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); the files are rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the access is as of 2026-10-06 (see access_as_of).

method: access.py counts the places with a mapped stop within 400 m and ts_m above 400 in each municipality and divides by the counted places.
source_detail: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026); stops from transport.json (the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feeds of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, and of municipal systems, read on 2026-10-02; OpenStreetMap extract of 1 October 2026) and feed end dates from operators.json; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: A high value means that the figure for any mapped stop (transit_pct) overstates the access that a published timetable supports. In the 2026-10 snapshot the value is 15.4% island-wide (3,717 of 24,209 places; about 32% of the 11,507 places near any mapped stop). It ranges from 0.0 to 94.9 (Juncos), and 45 of the 78 municipalities have a value above 0. Five municipalities have 50% or more because their feed has ended: Juncos 94.9, Ponce 79.4, San Lorenzo 78.1, Fajardo 70.5 and Caguas 61.1. A high value is not proof that service stopped: a feed can run out of dates while buses still run.
caveats: Renewing a feed moves the places near its stops out of this share and into acc_cur400_pct.

Stops that volunteers mapped can be missing, out of date or wrong; the observatory does not check them on the ground. Where the operator publishes no feed at all, the nearby stops are only volunteer-mapped ones.
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable, so they are not counted.

Straight-line distance, not a walking route (see municipalities.walk_rule_400m). The share by walking along mapped roads is in the acc_walk fields (acc_walk400_pct, acc_walk800_pct, acc_wfreq400_pct).
A municipality with few places can swing widely: the smallest has 36 places, so one place is 2.8 points. Check access_n before you compare shares.

A municipality with no stop counted inside its border (14 in the 2026-10 snapshot) holds the stored value: 0.0, or a small value where a place lies near a stop in a neighboring municipality (for example 0.5 for Toa Alta). That is not a measured 0%. The 2D map leaves it unshaded and unranked, and the downloaded municipality table leaves it blank.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: shade municipalities by % of places near only an expired or unscheduled stop
Map, Rankings tab: rank by % of places near only an expired or unscheduled stop
3D + Time page: municipality columns

example: In the 2026-10 snapshot: Juncos 94.9% (its feed ended 2026-07-31); Ponce 79.4%; San Juan 2.0%; Maricao 0.0% (no mapped stops).

name: Tourism places counted in the access shares (count)
plain: How many tourism places the access shares of the municipality are based on. It is the number each acc_ percentage divides by.
definition: The number of tourism places in the municipality that every access share (transit_pct and the acc_ fields) divides by: places with confidence 0.50 or higher and a type other than Places of Worship, located in the municipality. It is the same set as assets and equals assets in all 78 municipalities.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); the files are rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the access is as of 2026-10-06 (see access_as_of).

method: access.py counts the places on the default basis in each municipality when it computes the shares.
source_detail: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026; tourism places as classified by Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR)); stops and feed end dates from transport.json and operators.json (the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feeds of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, and of municipal systems, read on 2026-10-02); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: Read it before you compare shares: a share of a municipality with few places can swing widely. In the 2026-10 snapshot the values add up to 24,209 and range from 36 to 3,424 (San Juan). Multiply a share by this number and divide by 100 to get the number of places, to the nearest place. The Municipality tab's live tiles use the places that pass your filters, not this number.
caveats: Counts are listings from Overture Maps, not businesses, rooms or visitors.
A place outside every municipality boundary takes the municipality whose boundary is nearest (in the 2026-10 snapshot, the nearest center; see methods.municipality_assignment).
example: In the 2026-10 snapshot: San Juan 3,424; Ponce 1,041; Maricao 36.

name: Date the access fields are computed as of (date)
plain: The date against which the observatory judged whether each operator's timetable had ended when it computed the access fields. Quote it with any access figure.
definition: A date written YYYY-MM-DD. The observatory counts a stop as having a current timetable when its operator's feed end date is on or after this date. It applies to acc_cur400_pct, acc_cur800_pct, acc_freq400_pct, acc_sat400_pct, acc_sun400_pct, acc_paper_pct, stops_current and stops_expired. All 78 municipalities carry the same date. The same date is as_of in place_access.json and as_of in the access part of meta.json.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); the files are rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the access is as of 2026-10-06 (see access_as_of).

method: access.py sets it to the build date at a full build and to the run date in the nightly refresh. When a run changes no value, the files are not rewritten and the date does not move.
source_detail: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026; tourism places as classified by Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR)); stops and feed end dates from transport.json and operators.json (the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feeds of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, and of municipal systems, read on 2026-10-02); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot it is 2026-10-06, four days after the feeds were read (2026-10-02). A feed that ends after this date counts as current in the stored values. An older date means that no value has changed since then, not that the refresh did not run.
caveats: The stored values describe timetables on this date. They can be out of date by the time you read them if a feed has ended since and the next run has not written the change yet.
example: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 2026-10-06 in all 78 municipalities.

name: Residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop (count)
plain: How many residents of the municipality live within 400 m (a quarter mile), in a straight line, of a scheduled transit stop. It uses 2020 Census counts.
definition: Number of residents (2020 Census) who live in a Census block whose internal point (the point inside the block that the Census Bureau stores for it) is less than 401 m in a straight line from the nearest scheduled stop: the build rounds the distance down to whole meters, so a block up to 400.9 m away counts (see municipalities.pop_served_method). Scheduled stops are the boarding points in the timetable feeds of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and the municipal systems (field gtfs_stops), including feeds whose timetable has expired. The stop may lie in another municipality.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: network.py places each of the 36,570 populated 2020 Census blocks at its internal point (fields INTPTLAT and INTPTLON), finds the nearest scheduled stop (nearest by latitude and longitude) and adds the block's population to the municipality's total when the straight-line distance, rounded down to whole meters, is 400 or less. The municipality comes from the county code in the block's ID. See municipalities.pop_served_method.
source_detail: 2020 Census block population and internal points (TIGERweb Census2020 layer 10); ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and municipal GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stops
how_to_read: It estimates how many people live a short walk from a stop. It does not say whether a bus comes, how often, or where it goes. In the transit data built 2026-10-02, 925,788 of the island's 3,285,874 residents (28.2%) live within 400 m of a scheduled stop, and the value is 0 in 40 of the 78 municipalities: no scheduled stop lies within 400 m of any populated block.
caveats: Stops of expired timetables count. For stops with a timetable still running, see pop_served_active_pct.
Straight-line distance, not a walking route, and every resident of a block is placed at the block's internal point. See municipalities.pop_served_method.

Residents can be near a stop in the next municipality. In the transit data built 2026-10-02, Toa Alta (70), Naranjito (106), Arroyo (72) and Mayagüez (167) show residents served although no scheduled stop lies inside them.
Residents are 2020 Census counts and the stops are those of the transit data built 2026-10-02, so the count does not describe 2026 residents.
example: In the transit data built 2026-10-02: San Juan 276,909 of 342,259 residents; Humacao 2,794 of 50,896.

name: Residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop, expired timetables included (%)
plain: Out of every 100 residents of the municipality, how many live within 400 m (a quarter mile), in a straight line, of a scheduled transit stop. It uses the 2020 Census.
definition: pop_served_400m divided by the municipality's residents in the 2020 Census (the sum of its block populations, equal to population_2020 in all 78 municipalities), times 100, rounded to one decimal. Stops of expired timetables count.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: Residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop divided by all residents of the municipality, times 100. See municipalities.pop_served_method.
source_detail: 2020 Census block population (TIGERweb Census2020 layer 10); ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and municipal GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stops
how_to_read: A high value means most people live near a stop with a published timetable. It does not measure frequency, hours or destinations. A value of 0.0 means no populated block lies within 400 m of a scheduled stop; it does not mean the municipality has no transit users. The map shades it in five classes (quintiles) and the Municipality tab highlights values under 25%. In the transit data built 2026-10-02 the value ranges from 0.0 to 80.9 (San Juan) and is 28.2% island-wide. In that data 40 of the 78 municipalities have 0.0, so the lowest class holds all 40 and one class is empty; read the legend.
caveats: Stops of expired timetables count, so the share of residents near a stop with a current timetable is lower (see pop_served_active_pct).
Straight-line distance, not a walking route, and every resident of a block is placed at the block's internal point. See municipalities.pop_served_method.

Share of residents. For tourism places use acc_cur400_pct (a stop with a current timetable) or transit_pct (any mapped stop). The place measures and this one use different stop sets, and transit_pct also counts volunteer-mapped stops and stops of ended timetables, so compare like with like: pop_served_active_pct with acc_cur400_pct. In the transit data built 2026-10-02 Mayagüez shows 0.2% of residents, and 21.5% of tourism places by transit_pct but 4.2% by acc_cur400_pct.
Residents are 2020 Census counts and the stops are those of the transit data built 2026-10-02, so the share does not describe 2026 residents.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: shade municipalities by % of residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop (incl. expired timetables)
Map, Rankings tab: rank by % of residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop (incl. expired timetables)
Map, Municipality tab (click a municipality): Mobility section, residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop (shown only when pop_served_active_pct is missing)
3D + Time page: municipality columns

example: In the transit data built 2026-10-02: San Juan 80.9%; Ponce 56.6%; Humacao 5.5%; Maricao 0.0%.

name: Residents within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable (%)
plain: Out of every 100 residents, how many live within 400 m of a scheduled stop whose operator's timetable has not ended. It is pop_served_pct with the stops of ended timetables left out. The map calls this a stop with a current timetable.
definition: Residents (2020 Census) with at least one scheduled stop within 400 m, in a straight line, from an operator whose feed is active, divided by all residents of the municipality, times 100, rounded to one decimal. Active means the feed's status is not expired on the build date of the transit data: its last service end date is not earlier than that date (2026-10-02 in the current data). Feeds that are current, expiring or of unknown end date are active (see municipalities.feed_status); this includes feeds that expire soon. The observatory calls a stop of an active feed a stop with a current timetable. The tourism-place fields use the same idea (acc_cur400_pct and the other acc_ fields), with one difference: there a feed with no end date does not count. No feed lacks an end date in the 2026-10 snapshot.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: Same blocks and 400 m rule as pop_served_pct, but stops of operators whose feed status is expired are skipped when looking for a stop within reach. There is no matching count field.
source_detail: 2020 Census block population; GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stops of operators whose feed has not expired (ATI, Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, and municipal feeds)
how_to_read: Compare it with pop_served_pct. A big gap means most nearby stops belong to a timetable that has lapsed. A feed can run out of dates while buses still run, so a low value is not proof that service stopped. In the transit data built 2026-10-02, Ponce shows 56.6% and 0.0%; Caguas 42.4% and 3.5%; island-wide the share is 22.2%, against 28.2% for pop_served_pct. In that data the Canóvanas feed, which ends 2026-10-31, counts as active. The same 7 feeds are expired for residents (as of 2026-10-02) and for places (as of 2026-10-06). For the places near a stop with a current timetable, see acc_cur400_pct. The map labels this field 'of residents within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable'.
caveats: Judged on one date, the build date of the transit data (2026-10-02). A feed that ends a day later counts as active.
Straight-line distance, not a walking route, and every resident of a block is placed at the block's internal point. See municipalities.pop_served_method.

In Carolina and Manatí the value is slightly higher than pop_served_pct although it counts fewer stops, because the two tests find the nearest stop in different ways; see municipalities.pop_served_method.
Residents are 2020 Census counts and the stops are those of the transit data built 2026-10-02, so the share does not describe 2026 residents.

Map, Rankings tab: rank by % of residents within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable
Map, Municipality tab (click a municipality): Mobility section, residents within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable (whole percent; highlighted under 25%)

name: Residents within 400 m of an ATI stop (count)
plain: How many residents live within 400 m of at least one stop in the timetable of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), whose feed covers Tren Urbano, buses and ferries. It counts people, not a share.
definition: Number of residents (2020 Census) in blocks with at least one stop of the ATI feed within 400 m, in a straight line. The ATI feed covers Tren Urbano, the buses of the Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses (AMA) and the AcuaExpreso ferries. It can overlap with pop_served_muni: a person near both an ATI stop and a municipal stop is in both counts.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: For each populated block the build lists every scheduled stop within 400 m (straight line) and flags the block when one of them belongs to the ATI feed. Flagged blocks' populations are added by municipality. See municipalities.pop_served_method.
source_detail: 2020 Census block population; ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stops
how_to_read: Use it to see how much of a municipality's reach comes from the regional operator. Do not add it to pop_served_muni: people near both are counted twice. In the transit data built 2026-10-02, San Juan has 255,093 + 133,352, which is more than its 276,909 residents served, and the count is non-zero in 11 municipalities.
caveats: Straight-line distance, not a walking route, and every resident of a block is placed at the block's internal point. See municipalities.pop_served_method.
The ATI feed's timetable was valid at the 2026-10-02 build, so this count has no expired-feed effect.
Residents are 2020 Census counts and the stops are those of the transit data built 2026-10-02, so the count does not describe 2026 residents.
ATI provides its feed as is, without warranty, and its terms ask apps built on it to say they are not affiliated with ATI. The observatory is not affiliated with or sponsored by ATI.
example: In the transit data built 2026-10-02: San Juan 255,093; Bayamón 51,708; Ponce 0.

name: Residents within 400 m of a municipal stop (count)
plain: How many residents live within 400 m of at least one stop from a municipal transit system's timetable feed. It is a count of people, not a share.
definition: Number of residents (2020 Census) in blocks with at least one stop from any feed other than the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) feed within 400 m, in a straight line. These are the municipal feeds read by the observatory. Feeds whose timetable has expired are included. It can overlap with pop_served_ati.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: For each populated block the build lists every scheduled stop within 400 m (straight line) and flags the block when one of them belongs to a feed other than ATI. Flagged blocks' populations are added by municipality. See municipalities.pop_served_method.
source_detail: 2020 Census block population; municipal GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stops (National RTAP, Rural Transit Assistance Program, portal)
how_to_read: Use it to see how much of a municipality's reach comes from municipal systems. Do not add it to pop_served_ati: people near both are counted twice. In the transit data built 2026-10-02 the observatory reads 24 municipal feeds and the count is non-zero in 35 municipalities.
caveats: Includes residents served only by an expired timetable. In the transit data built 2026-10-02, 53,884 Caguas residents are near a municipal stop, and the Caguas feed ended 2026-01-31.
Straight-line distance, not a walking route, and every resident of a block is placed at the block's internal point. See municipalities.pop_served_method.
Residents are 2020 Census counts and the stops are those of the transit data built 2026-10-02, so the count does not describe 2026 residents.
The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it.
example: In the transit data built 2026-10-02: San Juan 133,352; Guaynabo 63,250; Ponce 77,833.

name: Municipal transit system: state of its public timetable
plain: Whether the municipality runs its own bus or trolley system that reports to the federal transit database, and whether its public timetable is still valid. Empty when no such system is listed.
definition: Status of the public timetable (GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, feed) of the municipal transit system that the National Transit Database (NTD) checklist lists for this municipality. The status comes from the feed's end date compared with the build date of the transit data (2026-10-02 in the current data): current when the end date is more than 60 days away, expired when it is earlier than the build date, none when the system is on the checklist but no public feed was found. The field is empty (null) when the observatory matched no municipal system from the checklist. The code also defines expiring (ends within 60 days), unknown (no end date) and broken (the feed could not be read).

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: network.py reads the list of Puerto Rico agencies in the National Transit Database of the Federal Transit Administration (through the Transitland Atlas copy of the 2023 table), keeps the agencies named for a municipality, and looks for a public GTFS feed of each in the registry of the National RTAP (Rural Transit Assistance Program) portal. For each feed it takes the latest end date among the service calendars and sets the status. build.py copies the status of the municipality's system into this field.
source_detail: FTA (Federal Transit Administration) NTD agency list via Transitland Atlas (2023 GTFS weblinks table); National RTAP (Rural Transit Assistance Program) portal registry

values.current: A timetable is published and its end date is more than 60 days after the build date.
values.expired: A timetable is published but its end date is before the build date, so its dates have run out.
values.none: The municipality's system is on the NTD checklist but no public timetable feed was found.
values.(empty): The observatory matched no municipal system to this municipality from the NTD checklist. Some municipalities whose feeds the observatory reads are in this group (see the caveats).

how_to_read: Current means a valid timetable is published. It does not mean buses run on time. Empty does not mean the municipality has no bus service: the checklist may not list its system. None means the observatory found no feed in the National RTAP registry; the municipality may publish a timetable elsewhere. The checklist is the federal 2023 reporting year, so a system that began or stopped later may be missing or listed in error. Current is judged on the latest end date of any service calendar in the feed, so it shows that some service is dated ahead, not that every route is valid. The Municipality tab shows current as "schedule published", expired as "schedule expired" and none as "no public schedule". In the 2026-10 snapshot, 14 municipalities show current, 7 expired, 15 none and 42 are empty; expiring, unknown and broken do not occur.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Cabo Rojo, Canóvanas and Corozal publish timetable feeds that the observatory reads (their stops count in gtfs_stops and pop_served_muni), but the observatory matches no NTD agency to them, so this field is empty and muni_system_routes is 0 for them.
The value is fixed at the build or nightly refresh. The Transit tab recomputes each feed's state from its end date whenever the page opens, so it can show expired where this field still says current.
Only one system is recorded per municipality.

view.label: Map, Municipality tab: Municipal system chip

example: In the 2026-10 snapshot: Guaynabo: current; Ponce: expired; Carolina: none; Maricao: empty.

name: Routes in the municipal system's feed (count)
plain: How many routes the municipality's own transit system lists in its public timetable feed. It is 0 when the municipality has no such feed.
definition: Number of routes in the feed of the municipal system matched to this municipality (see muni_system) that the observatory can draw on the map: each has a route shape in the feed, or a trip that visits at least two stops at different places. Routes with neither are skipped. The count covers the whole feed, including routes that leave the municipality. It is 0 when muni_system is empty or none.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: network.py reads the routes of each feed and keeps those it can draw. build.py copies the count of the municipality's system, or 0 when no system is matched.
source_detail: Municipal GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) feeds (National RTAP, Rural Transit Assistance Program, portal); NTD (National Transit Database) agency list
how_to_read: A higher number means more routes in the timetable. It does not measure trips, frequency or coverage. A feed whose timetable has expired still counts. In the 2026-10 snapshot the largest value is 11 (Guaynabo).
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, a municipality with a feed that is not matched to it (Cabo Rojo, Canóvanas, Corozal) shows 0 although its feed has routes.
Routes of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) feed are not counted here.
The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it.
example: In the 2026-10 snapshot: Guaynabo 11; San Juan 9; Vieques 1; Carolina 0.

name: Land area by land use plan group (km²)
plain: How many square kilometers of the municipality the 2015 land use plan puts in each of four groups: urban, urbanizable, ordinary rural and especially protected rural. Water and roads are left out.
definition: An object with up to four numbers, in square kilometers rounded to one decimal: urban, urbanizable, rustic (ordinary rural) and protected. Each is the summed area of the plan polygons of that group that the plan assigns to the municipality. A group is missing when the municipality has no polygon of that class. A value of 0.0 means a polygon exists but its area rounds to 0.0 km² (under 0.05 km²). Class codes: see municipalities.landuse_classes.
unit: km² of land by plan group

coverage.frequency: Fixed to the 2015 plan; recomputed only if the plan or the municipal list changes.

method: landuse.py reads the Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015 polygons, maps each class to a group, and sums each polygon's Shape_Area (square meters in the plan's projected coordinates) divided by 1,000,000 per municipality and group, using the municipality named in the plan. Water and road polygons are not summed. See land.put_statistics.
source_detail: Junta de Planificación, Plan de Uso de Terrenos (PUT 2015), version of 30 November 2015; attributes CLASIPUT (class), Municipio and Shape_Area

values.urbanizable: Land classed Suelo Urbanizable Programado (SURP) or Suelo Urbanizable No Programado (SURNP).
values.rustic: Land classed Suelo Rústico Común (SRC), ordinary rural land.
values.protected: Land classed Suelo Rústico Especialmente Protegido (SREP and its subtypes).

name: Kinds of transit feature: stop, scheduled stop, station, terminal
plain: The observatory sorts every stop, station, terminal, airport, taxi stand and charger into one of eight kinds. This entry says how a scheduled stop differs from a mapped one and which kinds each municipal count adds up.
definition: A scheduled stop is any boarding point from a timetable feed (GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification) of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) or of a municipal system; it can have the kind transit stop, bus station, rail station or ferry terminal. A mapped stop is a point that volunteers added to OpenStreetMap; the observatory keeps it only when it does not duplicate a scheduled stop. A station or terminal is a larger facility: scheduled stops become stations by name or by the mode of the routes that serve them, and OpenStreetMap stations come from tags. The municipal fields count the kinds as follows: transit_stops adds transit stop, bus stop, bus station, rail station and ferry terminal; gtfs_stops adds every kind whose source is a timetable feed; bus_stations, rail_stations, ferry_terminals, airports, taxi_stands and ev_charging count one kind each.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, which counts the stops in transport.json again (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: The rules that give each point its kind are in transit.stop_kind.
source_detail: GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) feeds (ATI, municipal), kinds set in network.py parse_gtfs; OpenStreetMap tags, kinds set in transport.py osm_kind; FAA airports via BTS (Bureau of Transportation Statistics) NTAD (National Transportation Atlas Database)
how_to_read: Read a count by its kind. A high transit_stops value mixes scheduled stops and volunteer-mapped stops; gtfs_stops isolates the stops that have a timetable; stops_current, stops_expired and stops_osm split transit_stops by the state of the timetable. In the 2026-10 snapshot, transit_stops is 4,360 (transit stop 3,781, bus stop 459, bus station 91, rail station 16, ferry terminal 13) and gtfs_stops is 3,847 (transit stop 3,781, 44 scheduled bus stations, 16 rail stations, 6 scheduled ferry terminals). For the other kinds see the Codes table of transit.stop_kind.
caveats: The code can also read helipads and bike-rental points from OpenStreetMap; none appear in the 2026-10 snapshot (see transit.stop_kind).
A scheduled stop becomes a bus station by its name only.

name: State of a transit timetable feed (current, expiring, expired, none)
plain: Each transit operator's public timetable is marked current, expiring, expired or none (no public feed found). The first three come from the timetable's end date. This entry defines the words current and active used in the transit fields.
definition: The state of an operator's timetable feed on the build date of the transit data (2026-10-02 in the current data). Current: the feed's end date is more than 60 days after the build date. Expiring: it ends within 60 days. Expired: the end date is earlier than the build date. None: the operator reports to the National Transit Database (NTD) but no public feed was found. In the pop_served_active_pct field, active means not expired, so current, expiring and unknown-date feeds are all active. The access fields of tourism places use a similar test: a stop has a current timetable when its operator's feed end date is on or after the date of the computation (access_as_of), so the current and expiring states both count and a feed with no end date does not. The end date is the latest end date among the feed's service calendars, or the feed's own end date when it has no calendar. The code also defines unknown (no end date) and broken (the feed could not be read).
geography: Puerto Rico (all operators in the transit data)

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: network.py computes the state for every operator each time it builds or refreshes the network. The Transit tab recomputes current, expiring and expired from the end date when the page opens, using Puerto Rico's date, so a page opened later can show a newer state than the file.
source_detail: End dates in the ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and municipal GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) feeds; operator list from the FTA (Federal Transit Administration) NTD

values.current: Timetable end date more than 60 days after the build date.
values.expiring: Timetable ends within 60 days of the build date.
values.expired: Timetable end date is before the build date.
values.none: On the NTD list but no public feed found.
values.in_ati: The buses of the Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses (AMA) and the ferries of the Maritime Transport Authority, whose stops and routes are inside the feed of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI).
values.community: Routes mapped by volunteers in OpenStreetMap, with no timetable (públicos and other routes).

how_to_read: A current feed has an end date more than 60 days away. The start date and holiday or other exceptions are not checked, and the end date is the latest of all the feed's calendars, so current does not show that every route runs on a valid timetable. It does not show that vehicles run on that timetable either. Expired means the dates ran out, which can happen while buses still run. In the transit data built 2026-10-02 there are 44 operators: 17 current (including the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, ATI), 1 expiring, 7 expired (all municipal), 16 none, 2 inside the ATI feed and 1 community. Unknown and broken do not occur. In the access fields, 'current timetable' covers the first two states: 18 feeds (17 current and 1 expiring, Canóvanas) against 7 expired.
caveats: Stops of expired feeds are still counted in gtfs_stops, transit_stops, stops_expired, transit_pct and pop_served_pct. They are left out of stops_current, the acc_ fields and pop_served_active_pct.

name: The 400 m walking rule
plain: The observatory treats a place or a block as near transit when a stop lies within 400 m (a quarter mile) in a straight line. This entry says which stops each measure uses.
definition: The observatory counts a place or a block as near transit when a stop lies 400 m or less away in a straight line. The distance is a planning assumption, not a measure of how far people walk. All fixed distances are listed in transit.distance_rules. The distance is measured to a stop in any municipality. The measures use the rule with different stop sets. The walking measures for tourism places (tw_m in place_access.json; acc_walk400_pct, acc_walk800_pct and acc_wfreq400_pct; the barrio counts acc_walk400 and acc_wfreq400) apply the same 400 m and 800 m to the distance walked along mapped roads instead of the straight line (see place_access.tw_m). Tourism places near any mapped stop (places_near_transit, transit_pct): the nearest stop, bus station, rail station or ferry terminal of transit_stops, scheduled or volunteer-mapped, from any feed including those that have ended. Tourism places near a stop with a current timetable (acc_cur400_pct, acc_freq400_pct, acc_sat400_pct and acc_sun400_pct; acc_cur800_pct uses 800 m): scheduled stops of operators whose feed has not ended on access_as_of, with the distance rounded up to whole meters. Residents (pop_served_400m, pop_served_pct, pop_served_active_pct, pop_served_ati, pop_served_muni): scheduled stops only, measured from each Census block's internal point; pop_served_active_pct skips expired feeds. The overall resident share rounds the distance down to whole meters before it tests 400 m (see municipalities.pop_served_method).

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: Distance in meters = square root of (dlat × 111,320)² plus (dlng × 111,320 × cos(mean latitude))², with dlat and dlng in degrees. A place is near when its nearest stop is 400 m or less away; for the nearest stop with a current timetable the distance is rounded up to whole meters (ts_m), so ts_m of 400 or less is the test. Against a computation in projected meters the formula is about 0.6% long north to south, so a share can read up to 0.1 point lower. For the overall resident share, a block is near when the distance to its nearest stop, rounded down to whole meters, is 400 or less. For the resident figures that count the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) feed, the municipal feeds or active feeds, a block is near when any stop of that group is 400 m or less away.
source_detail: transport.py and network.py (WALK_M = 400); access.py (NEAR_M = 400, FAR_M = 800)
how_to_read: Near means a short straight-line distance to a stop. It does not account for service frequency or hours, hills, rivers, fences, missing sidewalks or street crossings. A place 300 m from a stop across a highway counts as near.
caveats: The place measure acc_cur400_pct and the resident measure pop_served_active_pct both need a timetable that has not ended, so they can be compared. transit_pct also counts volunteer-mapped stops and stops of ended timetables, so it cannot be compared with the resident measures.
A distance is only as good as its points: a resident is placed at the block's internal point and a place at its listed coordinates.

name: How residents near a scheduled stop are counted
plain: Residents are placed by 2020 Census block, and a block counts as served when a scheduled stop lies within 400 m. This entry gives the steps and the known limits.
definition: The observatory takes the 36,570 Census blocks of Puerto Rico that had at least one resident in 2020 (3,285,874 people). Each block's population sits at the block's internal point, the point inside the block that the Census Bureau stores (fields INTPTLAT and INTPTLON). The block's municipality is read from the county code in its ID, so each municipality's total equals population_2020 in all 78 municipalities. For each block: served is true when the nearest scheduled stop, from any feed, any municipality, is less than 401 m away (the distance is rounded down to whole meters); active is true when a stop of an operator whose feed has not expired is 400 m or less away; ATI is true when a stop of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) feed is 400 m or less away; municipal is true when a stop of any other feed is 400 m or less away. Each field adds the populations of the blocks with the flag.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

method: network.coverage() runs in build.py and again in refresh_network.py. The overall served flag looks up the single nearest stop by latitude and longitude and rounds its distance in meters down to a whole number. The active, ATI and municipal flags look at every stop in a small search window around the block and then test the exact distance against 400 m, so the two tests can differ slightly.
source_detail: 2020 Census blocks (TIGERweb Census2020 layer 10); ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and municipal GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stops
how_to_read: The counts are estimates of how many people live near a stop. They treat everyone in a block as living at one point, so a large rural block with people spread along a road is approximated.
caveats: ATI plus municipal can exceed the overall count because people near both are counted in both. In the transit data built 2026-10-02, San Juan has 255,093 + 133,352 against 276,909 served.

The overall test and the other three tests differ slightly. In the transit data built 2026-10-02, recounting with exact distances gives 925,020 residents served island-wide instead of 925,788. 14 blocks (1,219 residents) count in the overall test only because their distance rounds down to 400 m. 4 blocks (451 residents) are missed because the nearest stop by coordinates is not the nearest in meters. The difference is under 1 percentage point in every municipality; the largest is Vega Baja (287 residents, 0.5 points).

In the transit data built 2026-10-02, pop_served_active_pct is higher than pop_served_pct in Carolina (58.1 against 57.9) and Manatí (30.4 against 30.3) for the same reason: it uses the exact distance.
Expired feeds count in the overall, ATI and municipal figures.

name: Which places each municipal percentage counts
plain: Two place counts are in use. Transit shares count tourism places. Land use plan shares of places count every place listing. This entry sets them side by side.
definition: Tourism places (field assets; used by transit_pct, places_near_transit and the acc_ shares, with access_n as the number counted): Overture Maps places that Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) classified into the observatory's categories and de-duplicated, with confidence 0.50 or higher and places of worship left out. All listings (used by places_on_protected_land, places_on_protected_land_pct and places_urban_pct): the same places with no confidence cut-off and with places of worship. In both cases a place belongs to the municipality where its point falls, not to the municipality in its address.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full snapshot build (Snapshot 2026-10); the plan itself dates from 2015.

method: build.py sets the municipality from each place's point and computes assets with the filter above. landuse.py receives the whole place list, without the filter, so its place counts and shares use all listings.
source_detail: Overture Maps places; build.py (MIN_CONF = 0.50) and landuse.py
how_to_read: Do not compare places_on_protected_land with assets or with in_protected directly: they count different sets of places. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 24,209 tourism places and 32,541 listings: the listings are the 24,209 tourism places plus 3,300 below confidence 0.50 and 5,032 places of worship.
caveats: The other place counts in municipalities.json (assets, in_sfha, in_protected, with_website, places_near_transit, access_n and the acc_ shares) use the tourism places basis; the three land use place fields are the exception.
The map's filters (confidence, categories, places of worship) change the places on screen, not these stored fields.

name: When the transit fields of a municipality are updated
plain: Most transit fields now follow the nightly refresh. A few change only when the whole snapshot is rebuilt. This entry says which.
definition: A full build (build.py) computes every transit field. A nightly job (refresh_network.py, which runs at 04:17 Puerto Rico time) re-reads the transit feeds. When a feed has changed, it rewrites in municipalities.json the fields pop_served_400m, pop_served_pct, pop_served_active_pct, pop_served_ati, pop_served_muni, muni_system and muni_system_routes, and the scheduled stops in transport.json. Every night, whether or not a feed changed, it then runs access.py, which recomputes from the stops file and rewrites only what changed: in municipalities.json the stop counts (transit_stops, gtfs_stops, bus_stations, rail_stations, ferry_terminals, airports, public_airports, taxi_stands, ev_charging, stops_current, stops_expired and stops_osm), places_near_transit, transit_pct, access_n, access_as_of and the acc_ fields; place_access.json; the transit_m, transit_400m and nearest_stop fields of places.json; and the access block and the count transport.places_near_transit in meta.json. It does not rebuild barrios.geojson (the barrio counts), the OpenStreetMap stops, the airports of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), the Uber listing or the other fields of places.json. Those change at the next full build.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (the transit data of the 2026-10 snapshot were built on 2026-10-02; the access fields are as of 2026-10-06).

method: Fields rewritten at night are recomputed from the feeds read that night (refresh_network.py) and, through access.py, from the stops file. All other transit fields are computed only at a full build. The Transit tab recalculates feed states from their end dates in the browser, against the date when the page is opened.
source_detail: refresh_network.py (the nightly transit refresh)
how_to_read: Cite a transit field with the date of its data: the build date of the transit data (2026-10-02 in this snapshot) and, for the access fields, access_as_of (2026-10-06), not only the snapshot label, because the nightly refresh can change them without a new snapshot. The barrio counts are the exception: they keep the values of the last full build, so between full builds they can lag the municipality fields.
caveats: What the 2026-10 access update changed. The transit fields of places.json (transit_m, transit_400m and nearest_stop) and the stop counts of municipalities.json had gone out of date, so they were recomputed from today's stop list. 1,204 of the 35,118 places changed: the distance by more than 2 m for 892 and by 1 or 2 m for 152 (all shorter), and the stop name only for 160. 130 places gained the 400 m flag and none lost it; 129 of them are in Jayuya, whose 58 stops had a longitude without its minus sign when the places were last measured (all 183 places in Jayuya changed). Stop counts changed in six municipalities: Jayuya 0 to 54, Culebra 59 to 1, Utuado 47 to 50, Caguas 304 to 305, Juncos 129 to 128 and San Lorenzo 158 to 159. The share of places near any mapped stop changed in Jayuya (0.0 to 70.7) and Ponce (79.0 to 79.1). On the default basis the island count went from 12,369 places (46.5%) to 12,481 (47.0%). The residents-served fields did not change.
The access fields keep the date of the last run that changed a value (access_as_of). A run that finds no change writes nothing, so an older date does not mean that the refresh did not run.

name: Land use plan classes and groups
group: Land use plan: classes and methods
plain: The 2015 land use plan labels each piece of land with a class code. The observatory gathers the codes into six groups: urban, urbanizable, ordinary rural, protected, water and road. The land-area shares use the first four groups; the place shares keep water and road polygons in the denominator.
definition: The Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015 (PUT 2015, Junta de Planificación) gives each polygon a class code (CLASIPUT). The observatory gathers the codes into six groups: urban (SU, Suelo Urbano), urbanizable (SURP, Suelo Urbanizable Programado, and SURNP, Suelo Urbanizable No Programado), ordinary rural (SRC, Suelo Rústico Común), protected (SREP, Suelo Rústico Especialmente Protegido, and every SREP subtype), water (AGUA) and road (VIAL). The land-area shares (landuse_km2, urban_pct, urbanizable_pct, rustic_common_pct, protected_land_pct) use the first four groups only. The place shares (places_on_protected_land_pct, places_urban_pct) keep water and road polygons in the denominator. Every code and its meaning is in land.cls.

coverage.frequency: Fixed to the 2015 plan; recomputed only if the plan or the municipal list changes.

method: landuse.py upper-cases the CLASIPUT code, looks it up in a table (GROUPS) and, when the code is not in the table, tries the part before the first hyphen.
source_detail: Junta de Planificación, PUT 2015 (CLASIPUT, DESCRIPPUT); landuse.py GROUPS
how_to_read: Urban, urbanizable and ordinary rural are the plan's general classes; the SREP codes add the reason for protection. Read the plan itself for what each class allows. In the 2015 plan, landuse.geojson holds 996 polygons; 68 of them carry the five less common subtypes (SREP-AE, SREP-AP, SREP-EA, SREP-EP, SREP-P).
caveats: Class meanings follow the plan's names; they are not legal advice and do not say what a given parcel may be used for.
The Plan's own version fields read PUT-2014 and 30-NOV-2015; this dictionary calls the version dated 30 November 2015 PUT 2015 (see land.put_layer).

The Junta de Planificación states no data license, and its site footer reads "Todos los derechos reservados". Check its terms before reusing the plan or figures computed from it. The Junta's page (read 2026-10-03) gives the plan a ten-year term and lists a review process for a new plan (PUT-2025). These classes describe the 2015 plan only.
